# Incorporating LaTex output from Stata

## Table commands

*Table* command is provides a basis to create customized tables for descriptive statistics. However, we can use the *collect* command after the *table* command to export our results into various documents of our choice.

We have seen the table command before, but let's look at some frequency tables using the *table* command. We use *statistics(frequency)* as the option
```{stata table1, eval=FALSE}
table (industry) (union), statistic(frequency) 
```

```{stata table1_1, echo=FALSE}
quietly use "/Users/Sam/Desktop/Econ 643/Bookdown/Week10/week10_cps_example.dta"
table (industry) (union), statistic(frequency) 
```

Next, let's add percentages along with frequencies with *statistic(percent)*.
```{stata table2, eval=FALSE}
table (industry) (union), statistic(frequency) statistic(percent)
```

```{stata table2_1, echo=FALSE}
quietly use "/Users/Sam/Desktop/Econ 643/Bookdown/Week10/week10_cps_example.dta"
table (industry) (union), statistic(frequency) statistic(percent)
```

Let's add mean, median, and standard deviation with statistic(mean <var>) statistic(median <var>) and statistic(sd <var>) as options.
```{stata table3, eval=FALSE}
table (industry) (union) () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings)
```

```{stata table3_1, echo=FALSE}
quietly use "/Users/Sam/Desktop/Econ 643/Bookdown/Week10/week10_cps_example.dta"
table (industry) (union) () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings)
```

### Nesting within rows

We can nest the two categorical variables within rows instead of one categorical being rows and the other categorical being columns.

```{stata table4, eval=FALSE}
table (industry union) () () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings) nototals
```

```{stata table4_1, echo=FALSE}
quietly use "/Users/Sam/Desktop/Econ 643/Bookdown/Week10/week10_cps_example.dta"
table (industry union) () () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings) nototals
```

We can flip the nesting order by reversing the variable order within the row parantheses.

```{stata table5, eval=FALSE}
table (union industry) () () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings) nototals
```

```{stata table5_1, echo=FALSE}
quietly use "/Users/Sam/Desktop/Econ 643/Bookdown/Week10/week10_cps_example.dta"
table (union industry) () () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings) nototals
```

### Nesting within columns

We can nest the two categorical variables within columns as well.

```{stata table6, eval=FALSE}
table () (union sex) () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings) nototals
```

```{stata table6_1, echo=FALSE}
quietly use "/Users/Sam/Desktop/Econ 643/Bookdown/Week10/week10_cps_example.dta"
table () (union sex) () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings) nototals
```

We can reverse the order of the nesting within columns as well.

```{stata table7, eval=FALSE}
table () (sex union) () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(percent) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings) nototals
```

```{stata table7_1, echo=FALSE}
quietly use "/Users/Sam/Desktop/Econ 643/Bookdown/Week10/week10_cps_example.dta"
table () (sex union) () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(percent) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings) nototals
```

### Customize the format

We can customize the formats with *sformat* to add string characters and *nformat* to format the numerics.

```{stata table8, eval=FALSE}
table () (sex union) () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(percent) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings) nototals nformat(%6.2f  mean sd median) sformat("$%s" mean sd median) sformat("%s%%" percent)
```

```{stata table8_1, echo=FALSE}
quietly use "/Users/Sam/Desktop/Econ 643/Bookdown/Week10/week10_cps_example.dta"
table () (sex union) () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(percent) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings) nototals nformat(%6.2f  mean sd median) sformat("$%s" mean sd median) sformat("%s%%" percent)
```

## Collect commands

Stata has a collection of *collect* commands to help you format and export your descriptive statistics after the *table* command.

We can preview our table comments with the *collect preview* command.
```{stata collect1, eval=FALSE}
collect preview
```

```{stata collect1_1, echo=FALSE}
quietly{
use "/Users/Sam/Desktop/Econ 643/Bookdown/Week10/week10_cps_example.dta"
table () (sex union) () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(percent) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings) nototals nformat(%6.2f  mean sd median) sformat("$%s" mean sd median) sformat("%s%%" percent)
}
collect preview
```

We can change our labels if we want with the *modify* option. We can check the change with the *collect label list <var>* command.
```{stata collect2, eval=FALSE}
collect label dim sex "Sex of Individual", modify
collect label list sex
collect preview
```

```{stata collect2_1, echo=FALSE}
quietly{
use "/Users/Sam/Desktop/Econ 643/Bookdown/Week10/week10_cps_example.dta"
table () (sex union) () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(percent) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings) nototals nformat(%6.2f  mean sd median) sformat("$%s" mean sd median) sformat("%s%%" percent)
}
collect label dim sex "Sex of Individual", modify
collect label list sex
collect preview
```

Let's modify the other variable, too.
```{stata collect3, eval=FALSE}
collect label dim union "Union Status", modify
collect label list union
collect preview
```

```{stata collect3_1, echo=FALSE}
quietly{
use "/Users/Sam/Desktop/Econ 643/Bookdown/Week10/week10_cps_example.dta"
table () (sex union) () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(percent) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings) nototals nformat(%6.2f  mean sd median) sformat("$%s" mean sd median) sformat("%s%%" percent)
collect label dim sex "Sex of Individual", modify
}
collect label dim union "Union Status", modify
collect label list union
collect preview
```

We can use the *collect dims* command to get the collect dimensions.
```{stata collect4, eval=FALSE}
collect dims
collect label list result, all
```

```{stata collect4_1, echo=FALSE}
quietly{
use "/Users/Sam/Desktop/Econ 643/Bookdown/Week10/week10_cps_example.dta"
table () (sex union) () if prerelg==1, statistic(frequency) statistic(percent) statistic(mean earnings) statistic(sd earnings) statistic(median earnings) nototals nformat(%6.2f  mean sd median) sformat("$%s" mean sd median) sformat("%s%%" percent)
collect label dim sex "Sex of Individual", modify
collect label dim union "Union Status", modify
}
collect dims
collect label list result, all
```

We can export our descriptive statistics table into various formats.
Let's export to LaTex.
```{stata collect5, eval=FALSE}
collect export example.tex, replace
```

Let's use *collect export* into Markdown.
```{stata collect6, eval=FALSE}
collect export example.md, replace
```

Let's use *collect export* into Excel. We have additional commands with *putexcel* to generate a report template and then use *collect export* to export the descriptive statistics table.
```{stata collect7, eval=FALSE}
collect export example.xlsx, replace
```

Let's use *collect export* into MS Word. We have additional commands with *putdocx* to generate a report template and then use *collect export* to export the descriptive statistics table.

```{stata collect8, eval=FALSE}
collect export example.docx, replace
```

There is also a suite of commands with *putpdf* to export tables into a pdf file
